summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would add 2018-19 funding for government activities outside ordinary annual services, including capital investment, new administered outcomes and assistance to other governments.
It would restore the Finance Minister's available advance to $380 million, disregarding earlier allocations so that further urgent expenditure could be funded during the financial year.
The legislation would commence on Royal Assent and repeal on 1 July 2021, alongside separate additional-estimates bills covering ordinary government services and parliamentary departments.
changes: Appropriations would be reduced where the Finance Minister had already advanced money for the same expenditure.
Departmental equity injections would provide funding for asset investment, including heritage and cultural assets at designated collecting institutions.
Corporate Commonwealth entity funding would be paid through the relevant department for the receiving entity's purposes.
Transfers between specified Commonwealth entities would count against appropriations as though they were actual payments.
summary.affected: Commonwealth entities, the Finance Minister and state, territory and local governments receiving the scheduled assistance are affected.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The government introduced additional estimates appropriation bills totalling over $2.5 billion, including $626 million for Health (aged care royal commission and drought assistance), nearly $600 million for Home Affairs (national security, refugee aid, disaster preparedness), $100.5 million for Infrastructure, $89.8 million for Agriculture (both drought assistance), $60 million for the Attorney-General’s Department (aged care royal commission), $60 million for the Australian Sports Commission (community sport and Tokyo Olympics), and $14 million for the National Gallery.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The speaker moved the second reading of Appropriation Bill (No. 4) 2018‑2019, seeking approval for $752.9 million in additional appropriations. Key allocations include $82 million for security upgrades to Australia's overseas diplomatic network, $40.6 million for the Welfare Payment Infrastructure Transformation program, and $28 million for next generation visa processing systems.

speeches.speaker: Jim Chalmers
speeches.brief: Labor will not block the appropriation bills but argues the government has mismanaged finances, citing net debt more than doubled to $360 billion, gross debt at $543.3 billion, and an $11 billion increase under Prime Minister Morrison.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The appropriation bills provide funding for the Royal Commission into Aged Care Quality and Safety, drought assistance for farmers and farm communities, and security infrastructure enhancements for Australia's overseas diplomatic network.
